title: Occupancy-guided attention pathfinder and kernel autotuner
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Problem: Our current kernel selection primarily uses static heuristics tuned to a few canonical architectures and typical sequence lengths. Mixed workloads (short chat turns + occasional long prefill requests) and heterogeneous customer hardware are producing suboptimal kernel choices: either higher cost or P95 latency regressions for corner cases.

Goal: Implement an occupancy-guided attention pathfinder that: (1) builds cheap per-architecture occupancy / memory-pressure fingerprints, (2) maps those fingerprints + sequence-length buckets to kernel candidates, and (3) runs a low-overhead online autotuner that explores and solidifies the best kernel for a given request class. Must support switching between prefill/ decode paths mid-request when evidence indicates a different kernel yields better end-to-end latency/cost.

Scope: runtime kernel selection, attention kernel variants, prefill vs decode scheduling logic, minimal probe microbench harness, telemetry definitions, and a staged rollout (canary -> A/B -> full). Not in scope: model rearchitecting or changes to kernel implementations themselves (other tickets exist for kernel micro-optimizations).
acceptance_criteria: Automated autotuner produces a per-arch + seqlen mapping that reduces median tokens-per-dollar by >=4% on mixed workloads compared to master in bench env
P95 tail latency when the autotuner is enabled does not regress more than 5% for 99% of requests (canary validated), with rollback path defined
Runtime emits new telemetry: kernel_fingerprint_id, probe_latency_ms, chosen_kernel_id, policy_version, switch_reason; metrics wired into per-model dashboards
Canary rollout steps and AB experiment (50/50) implemented with experiment flags in config and documented in runbook
End-to-end tests for mid-request switching across prefill->decode path with persisted KV cache correctness
implementation_notes: Fingerprint: lightweight tuple (gpu_arch, sm_count, free_mem_bucket, preferred_blocksize_hint, typical_prefill_kv_bytes) computed at agent boot and periodically refreshed
Seqlen bucketing: {short: <=64, medium: 65-512, long: >512} configurable per-customer; buckets map to a ranked kernel candidate list

Probe strategy: use sporadic microbatches (1-2 warmup iterations, 8-16 probe tokens) sampled at low rate (default 0.5% of requests) per fingerprint+bucket to estimate real throughput and occupancy impact
Exploration policy: epsilon-greedy with annealing schedule and forced periodic re-probing (to adapt to thermal throttling or driver upgrades), default epsilon=0.1 -> 0.02 over 24h
Mid-request switching: monitor kv cache growth and token-generation slope; switch candidates only at decode boundaries and only if predicted latency improvement > switch_cost + safety_margin
Safety: enforce latency SLO guardrails via a simple regret tracker; if autotuner causes >2% requests to breach SLO, automatically reduce exploration rate and roll back last policy change

Data capture: synthetic microbench results saved to S3 path s3://redwood-perf/auto-tune/ENG-41207/<date>/, microprobe traces to perf-trace service, and per-request metadata to instrumentation pipeline
Integration points: kernel catalog service (read/write candidate weights), runtime scheduler (selection hook), console (dashboard filters), rollout flag to toggle autotuner
Tests: unit tests for fingerprint creation, integration tests for probe harness, end-to-end tests with short/long mixed workload replay via bench harness
milestones: Spike and microprobe implementation (done) - perf/mini-results attached
Canary rollout and live metrics collection (target 2026-03-20)
updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete. Microprobe harness implemented and validated on gpus: A100-40GB, A10G. Observed occupancy differences up to 22% between kernels for long-prefill workloads.
2026-02-22: Design review completed. PM and Security reviewed telemetry schema; reduced retention for per-request traces to address PII concerns. Added opt-out flag per-customer.
2026-02-28: Prototype autotuner reduced cost-per-token by ~6% on mixed bench (short:70%, long:30%). P95 latency neutral for short requests; slight improvement on long prefill paths.
2026-03-03: Implemented kernel_fingerprint_id and candidate list CRUD in kernel catalog. Integration tests added.
2026-03-08: QA found a race when switching mid-request on models with very small KV stores. Added a mutex and a validation gate; CI added targeted test (kv-consistency-switch).

2026-03-10: Canary started (10% of traffic) in us-west-2 for runtime-1.22. Early telemetry shows probe latency overhead ~0.2ms p50 and negligible p95 impact. Next: expand canary and run 48h stability run.
